The orchestra manifest

Source: R/manifest_class.R
orchestra_manifest.Rd

A versioned, integrity-hashed, provenance-tracked record of one inference. It is the single result type components exchange: an emitter fills it in once, and every downstream consumer reads the same properties in the same places whatever produced them.

Usage

orchestra_manifest(
  manifest_version = "2.0.0-draft",
  emitter_package = character(0),
  emitter_version = character(0),
  inferential_target = character(0),
  run_id = character(0),
  method = character(0),
  seed = NA_integer_,
  params = data.frame(),
  outputs = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  obs_target = NULL,
  obs_schema = NULL,
  summary = NULL,
  consumed_manifests = list(),
  metadata = list(),
  timestamp = .POSIXct(double(), tz = ""),
  data_hash = character(0)
)

Arguments

manifest_version

The contract version this object conforms to. Defaults to manifest_version(). A consumer refuses a version it does not accept rather than coercing across a schema boundary.

emitter_package

The name of the component that emitted this manifest, as a single string.

emitter_version

The version of the emitting component, as a single string.

inferential_target

What the manifest is about. Must be one of inferential_targets().

run_id

A single non-empty string identifying this run. Emitters commonly derive it from a truncated payload digest so that it is stable under re-emission of the same result.

method

A single string naming the method that produced the result, conventionally qualified by its component, as in "PESTO:ies_callback".

seed

The integer RNG seed behind the result, or NA_integer_ when the result is deterministic or the seed is unknown.

params

A data frame of parameter draws, one row per realisation. Defaults to an empty data frame, which suits a verdict manifest that carries its content in summary.

outputs

Model-predicted outputs at each parameter draw, or NULL when the manifest carries no ensemble payload.

weights

Observation weights, or NULL.

obs_target

The observed targets the model was compared against, or NULL.

obs_schema

A semantic descriptor of the observation columns, giving each one a quantity and a unit, or NULL. Populating it activates the correspondence guard in assert_obs_schema_correspondence().

summary

A manifest_summary() holding the headline verdict, or NULL for an ensemble manifest that has no verdict to state.

consumed_manifests

A list of provenance handles, each as returned by manifest_lineage(), for the upstream manifests this result was derived from. Required to be non-empty when metadata$derived is TRUE.

metadata

A named list of caller-supplied metadata. The element derived is load-bearing: setting it to TRUE turns on the lineage requirement.

timestamp

A POSIXct emission time.

data_hash

The payload digest, as a single "sha256:<hex>" string. Emitters compute it over the payload slots; verify_manifest() recomputes and compares.

Value

An orchestra_manifest object.

Details

The properties fall into four groups. Identity (manifest_version, emitter_package, emitter_version, run_id, method, timestamp) says what this is and what made it. Semantics (inferential_target, obs_schema) says what it is about, in a closed vocabulary a consumer can dispatch on. Payload (params, outputs, weights, obs_target, summary, seed) carries the load-bearing content, and is exactly the set covered by data_hash. Provenance (consumed_manifests, metadata) records what this result was derived from.

Two rules are enforced by the validator rather than left to convention. A manifest whose metadata$derived is TRUE must record at least one entry in consumed_manifests: an approximation may never silently drop the lineage of the thing it approximated. And a summary, when set, must be a manifest_summary() object, so a verdict has a typed home instead of riding in params as a single-row pseudo-parameter table.

The data_hash deliberately covers the payload only. The schema version, the emitter identity and the timestamp are metadata, so re-tagging a manifest does not invalidate a payload that has not changed, while any edit to the payload is detected by verify_manifest().

Class identity across homes

The contract began as a script sourced into a workspace, where the class was created outside any package and its class vector reads c("orchestra_manifest", "S7_object"). Defined inside this package the same class is package-qualified and reads c("orchestraManifest::orchestra_manifest", "S7_object"), and components that emit a manifest without depending on this package still mint the bare form. Both are the same contract. Consumers in this package therefore test identity with is_orchestra_manifest(), which accepts either, rather than with a strict class check that would reject every manifest emitted outside this package.

See also

verify_manifest() and consume_manifest() for the integrity and schema guards, as_orchestra_manifest() for the emitter generic.

Author

Max Moldovan

Examples

m <- orchestra_manifest(
  emitter_package = "example",
  emitter_version = "0.1.0",
  inferential_target = "parameters",
  run_id = "example-001",
  method = "example:demo",
  seed = 1L,
  params = data.frame(a = c(0.1, 0.2), b = c(1.5, 1.4)),
  timestamp = as.POSIXct("2026-07-05 09:00:00", tz = "UTC"),
  data_hash = "sha256:not-yet-computed"
)
m@emitter_package
#> [1] "example"
